name: Tigran Petrosian
milestone_by_age_26: Awarded the Grandmaster title in 1952 at age 23, and placed 5th in the 1953 Candidates Tournament in Zurich, qualifying among the world's top chess players.
early_history_summary: Petrosian learned chess at age 8 in Tbilisi and began formal training at 12 under Archil Ebralidze at the Tiflis Palace of Pioneers. Orphaned during WWII, he swept streets to survive while continuing to study chess, winning the USSR Junior Championship in 1946 and 1947, and becoming a master by 1947.
family_context_summary: Born to Armenian parents in Tbilisi; father was illiterate and worked as a street cleaner. Orphaned during WWII, forcing young Petrosian to sweep streets to survive.
primary_early_advantage_tags: orphaned, Palace of Pioneers training, mentor Ebralidze, adversity, early specialization
evidence_summary: Petrosian was orphaned during WWII and survived by sweeping streets, yet managed to train at the Tiflis Palace of Pioneers under Archil Ebralidze from age 12. He won the USSR Junior Championship at 17 and became a master by 18. By 23, he was awarded the Grandmaster title and by 24 competed in the 1953 Candidates Tournament. His path was defined by adversity and self-created domain repetition rather than family advantage.

name: Masao Ono
milestone_by_age_26: Won the 1949 Emperor's Cup with University of Tokyo LB at age 26, the top football cup competition in Japan.
early_history_summary: Ono attended Shonan High School and then the University of Tokyo, where he played for the university's football team. After graduation, he joined Nissan Chemical while continuing to play for University of Tokyo LB, a team of University of Tokyo players and graduates.
primary_early_advantage_tags: University of Tokyo, Emperor's Cup, team sport
evidence_summary: Ono played football at the University of Tokyo, one of Japan's most elite institutions, and continued with the university's alumni team (University of Tokyo LB). At age 26, he won the 1949 Emperor's Cup, Japan's top football cup competition. Little is documented about his family background or early training.

name: Björn Borg
milestone_by_age_26: Won his first Grand Slam title at the 1974 French Open at age 18, and went on to win 11 Grand Slam titles by age 25, including 5 consecutive Wimbledon championships (1976-1980).
early_history_summary: Borg started playing tennis at age 9 after his father won a golden tennis racket at a table-tennis tournament. He trained with Sweden's leading coach Percy Rosberg at the Salk Club in Stockholm, and by 15 was representing Sweden in the Davis Cup. He turned professional in 1973 and won his first French Open at 18.
family_context_summary: Born to Rune Borg, an electrician, and Margaretha Borg in Stockholm. Grew up in the industrial town of Södertälje. His parents supported his tennis pursuit but were not wealthy.
parent_family_domain_summary: Not documented in reviewed sources. His father was an electrician who won a tennis racket at a table-tennis tournament, which sparked Borg's interest in tennis.
primary_early_advantage_tags: early tennis start, coach Rosberg, Davis Cup at 15, physical talent, topspin innovation
evidence_summary: Borg started playing tennis at 9 with a racket his father won, and by his early teens was beating players five years older. He trained with Sweden's top coach Percy Rosberg at the Salk Club in Stockholm, commuting after school. At 15, he debuted for Sweden in the Davis Cup, and at 18 he won his first French Open. His parents were working-class (father an electrician) but supported his training. His physical talent and revolutionary topspin game were evident from an early age.

name: Davor Šuker
milestone_by_age_26: Won the 1987 FIFA U-20 World Cup with Yugoslavia at age 19 (scoring 6 goals in 6 matches), and by 25-26 was among the top scorers in La Liga with 24 goals in the 1993-94 season for Sevilla.
early_history_summary: Šuker began playing football at NK Osijek in 1984 at age 16, quickly becoming the league's top scorer. He moved to Dinamo Zagreb in 1989, scored 34 goals in 60 matches, and was called up to the Yugoslavia national team. He joined Sevilla in 1991 and became one of La Liga's top scorers.
family_context_summary: Born in Osijek to a Bosnian Croat family from Livno. His father Tomislav was an accomplished shotputter who won gold at the Mediterranean Games. His sister Nevenka was a talented volleyball player.
parent_family_domain_summary: His father was an accomplished athlete (shotputter), suggesting a sporting family environment, though not specifically in football.
primary_early_advantage_tags: early football start, sporting family, FIFA U-20 World Cup, Osijek, war displacement
evidence_summary: Šuker grew up in a sporting family in Osijek — his father was a gold-medal shotputter and his sister a volleyball player. He started at NK Osijek at 16 and was discovered by a PE teacher who brought him to the club. He won the 1987 FIFA U-20 World Cup with Yugoslavia at 19, scoring 6 goals. The Croatian War displaced him to Sevilla in 1991, where he became one of La Liga's top scorers, netting 24 goals in the 1993-94 season at age 25-26.

name: Richard Dawkins
milestone_by_age_26: No material milestone by age 26 found. Dawkins earned his DPhil from Oxford in 1966 (age 25) and became an assistant professor at UC Berkeley in 1967 (age 26), but these are standard academic career steps. His material contributions — The Selfish Gene (1976), the meme concept, gene-centered view of evolution — all came after age 35.
early_history_summary: Dawkins attended Oundle School and then Balliol College, Oxford, where he studied zoology under Nikolaas Tinbergen. He earned his DPhil in 1966 and remained as a research assistant before moving to UC Berkeley as an assistant professor in 1967.
family_context_summary: Born in Nairobi, British Kenya. His father was a civil servant in the colonial agricultural service. The family returned to England in 1949. He attended Oundle School, a public school with a Church of England ethos.
parent_family_domain_summary: His father was an agricultural scientist in the colonial service, and Dawkins attended Oundle School and Oxford, suggesting a privileged educational background.
evidence_summary: Dawkins had a privileged educational path through Oundle School and Oxford, studying under Nobel laureate Nikolaas Tinbergen. He completed his DPhil at 25 and became an assistant professor at Berkeley at 26. However, these are standard academic career steps, not material milestones. His transformative work, The Selfish Gene, was published in 1976 when he was 35.

name: Anna Wintour
milestone_by_age_26: No material milestone by age 26 found. By 26, Wintour was a junior fashion editor at Harper's Bazaar in New York (fired after 9 months) and then a fashion editor at Viva magazine. Her material milestones — editor of British Vogue (1985), editor-in-chief of American Vogue (1988) — came in her late 30s.
early_history_summary: Wintour dropped out of North London Collegiate School at 18 and began working at Harper's & Queen in London in 1970 as an editorial assistant, helped by her father's connections. She moved to New York in 1975 as a junior fashion editor at Harper's Bazaar but was fired after nine months.
family_context_summary: Daughter of Charles Wintour, editor of the London Evening Standard. Her father's media connections helped her secure her first job at Harper's & Queen.
parent_family_domain_summary: Her father was a prominent newspaper editor who facilitated her entry into journalism through his connections.
evidence_summary: Wintour's entry into fashion journalism was facilitated by her father Charles Wintour, editor of the London Evening Standard, whose connections helped her land her first editorial assistant position at Harper's & Queen in 1970. By 26, she was a junior fashion editor at Harper's Bazaar in New York but was fired after nine months. Her material milestones came much later — editor of British Vogue at 36, editor-in-chief of American Vogue at 39.

name: Johnny Cash
milestone_by_age_26: Had multiple hit singles including 'Cry! Cry! Cry!' (1955, age 23) and 'I Walk the Line' (1956, age 24), which reached #1 on the Billboard country chart and crossed over to the pop charts, making him a major recording star by 26.
early_history_summary: Cash grew up in a poor farming family in Dyess, Arkansas, on a New Deal resettlement colony. He served in the US Air Force from 1950-1954, where he bought his first guitar and formed a band. After his service, he moved to Memphis, auditioned for Sun Records in 1954, and was signed, releasing his first hit 'Cry! Cry! Cry!' in 1955.
family_context_summary: Born to Ray and Carrie Cash, poor cotton farmers in Kingsland, Arkansas. The family moved to a Dyess Colony resettlement farm in 1935, living modestly. His mother introduced him to the guitar and the Church of God introduced him to music.
parent_family_domain_summary: Not documented in reviewed sources. His parents were cotton farmers with no music industry connections.
primary_early_advantage_tags: Sun Records, Memphis, rockabilly wave, poverty, Air Force, Tennessee Two
evidence_summary: Cash grew up in poverty on a New Deal farm colony in Arkansas, where his mother introduced him to guitar and church music. After Air Force service (1950-54), he moved to Memphis and auditioned for Sun Records, signing in 1954. His first hit 'Cry! Cry! Cry!' came in 1955 and 'I Walk the Line' reached #1 on the country chart in 1956, crossing over to pop. He rode the rockabilly/country wave from Memphis alongside Elvis Presley and Carl Perkins, with his band the Tennessee Two providing his distinctive sound.

name: Vince McMahon
milestone_by_age_26: No material milestone by age 26 found. By 26, McMahon had just joined his father's WWWF as a ring announcer and was assigned to promote a small card in Maine. His transformative milestone — buying the company from his father and building the national WWE empire — came in 1982 at age 37.
early_history_summary: McMahon didn't meet his father, wrestling promoter Vincent J. McMahon, until age 12. He graduated from East Carolina University in 1968 with a business degree, worked as a traveling salesman, and joined his father's WWWF in 1969 as a ring announcer. In 1971, he was assigned to a small territory in Maine.
family_context_summary: Son of Vincent J. McMahon, a wrestling promoter who owned the Capitol Wrestling Corporation. McMahon didn't meet his father until age 12 and grew up in a trailer park in North Carolina raised by his mother and grandmother.
parent_family_domain_summary: His father and grandfather were both wrestling promoters, giving McMahon eventual access to the industry, though he didn't meet his father until age 12.
evidence_summary: McMahon grew up without knowing his father (a wrestling promoter) until age 12, raised in a North Carolina trailer park. After college and a stint as a traveling salesman, he joined his father's WWWF in 1969 as a ring announcer. By 26, he had only been assigned to promote a small card in Maine. His transformative achievement — buying the company and building WWE into a national empire — came at 37 in 1982.

name: Ravi Shankar
milestone_by_age_26: Completed seven years of intensive sitar training under legendary musician Allauddin Khan by 1944 (age 24), made his public debut in 1939 (age 19), and was composing music for IPTA ballets and performing concerts throughout India by age 25-26.
early_history_summary: Shankar toured Europe and India as a dancer with his brother Uday Shankar's troupe from age 10. At 18, he gave up dancing to study sitar under Allauddin Khan in the traditional gurukul system, living with Khan's family for seven years. He made his public sitar debut in 1939 and completed training in 1944, then began composing and performing.
family_context_summary: Born to a Bengali Brahmin family in Benares. His father was a Middle Temple barrister and scholar who served as dewan of Jhalawar State. His eldest brother Uday Shankar was a celebrated dancer who took Ravi on tour at age 10.
parent_family_domain_summary: His brother Uday Shankar was a pioneering dancer who provided direct entry into the performing arts world. His father was a barrister and scholar, though Ravi was largely raised by his mother after his father left.
primary_early_advantage_tags: brother Uday Shankar, gurukul training, Allauddin Khan, international touring, Bengali cultural elite
evidence_summary: Shankar's eldest brother Uday, a celebrated dancer, took 10-year-old Ravi on international tours, exposing him to Paris, Monte Carlo, and Hollywood. At 18, Shankar left dancing to study sitar under Allauddin Khan in the traditional gurukul system for seven years, living with Khan's family and studying alongside Ali Akbar Khan. He made his public debut at 19, completed training at 24, and was composing for IPTA ballets and performing concerts by 25-26. His father was a barrister and scholar, giving the family cultural and intellectual standing.

evidence_summary: Ri Kwang-hyok was a regular left-back for the North Korea national team from 2007, accumulating 29+ caps by age 26. name: Jack Brabham
milestone_by_age_26: Won the Australian Speedcar Championship in 1949 (age 23) and the Australasian hillclimb title in 1951 (age 25), establishing himself as a top racing driver in Australia before moving to Formula One.
early_history_summary: Brabham left school at 15 to work in a garage and study engineering. He served as a RAAF flight mechanic from 1944-1946, then opened his own repair business. He started racing midget speedcars in 1948, winning the New South Wales Championship in his first season and the Australian Speedcar Championship the following year.
family_context_summary: Born in Hurstville, New South Wales. His father ran a grocery business and taught Jack to drive at age 12. The family was not wealthy but had a practical, mechanical background.
parent_family_domain_summary: Not documented in reviewed sources. His father had a grocery business, not a motorsport connection.
primary_early_advantage_tags: mechanical engineering, midget cars, self-built cars, Ron Tauranac partnership, Australian racing
evidence_summary: Brabham grew up around cars and mechanics, learning to drive at 12 and leaving school at 15 to work in a garage while studying engineering. After RAAF service as a mechanic, he opened his own repair business and began racing midget speedcars in 1948. He won the NSW Championship in his first season and the Australian Speedcar Championship at 23. His engineering skills allowed him to build and modify his own cars, and he formed a crucial partnership with Ron Tauranac. By 25, he won the Australasian hillclimb title.

name: Alan Rickman
milestone_by_age_26: No material milestone by age 26 found. By 26, Rickman was a graphic designer who had just applied to RADA. His professional acting career began at 28 (1974), his breakthrough came at 36 (Barchester Chronicles, 1982), and his film debut at 42 (Die Hard, 1988).
early_history_summary: Rickman studied graphic design at Chelsea College of Art (1965-68) and the Royal College of Art (1968-70), then opened a graphic design studio called Graphiti with friends. After three years, he decided to pursue acting and applied to RADA at age 26, attending from 1972 to 1974.
family_context_summary: Born in Brentford, London. His father was a factory worker who died when Rickman was 8. His mother raised him and his siblings alone. He attended Latymer Upper School on a scholarship.
parent_family_domain_summary: Not documented in reviewed sources. His family was working-class; his father was a factory worker.
evidence_summary: Rickman grew up in a working-class family in London; his father died when he was 8. He excelled at calligraphy and watercolour painting, attending Chelsea College of Art and the Royal College of Art for graphic design. He ran a successful graphic design studio (Graphiti) for three years before deciding to pursue acting at 26, applying to RADA. His professional acting career didn't begin until 28, with his breakthrough coming at 36.
